title: Upgrade readiness: compatibility simulator and rollback rehearsal
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build a deterministic "compatibility simulator" that exercises a candidate runtime+model bundle through the full preflight surface for LTS and non-LTS channels and produces a machine-readable pass/fail report and human-friendly runbook. The simulator combines: 1) compatibility probes for networked APIs and pinned SDK versions, 2) synthetic traffic generator that replicates production sequence-length distribution and KV/cache warmup patterns, 3) perf regression gates (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per token), 4) quality eval suite (prompt sets + automated scoring for hallucination/regression against baseline), and 5) an automated staged-rollback rehearsal that verifies the rollback path and migration safety on a staging cluster. The goal is to enable a single preflight action that surfaces regressions early and produces actionable remediation steps (e.g., fallback model variant, quantization profile tweak, or autoscaling policy change).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can run a configured LTS and non-LTS job and emit a JSON report with pass/fail and metric deltas.
Perf gates: p95 latency and tokens/sec thresholds are evaluated and flagged when regressions >10% vs baseline.
Quality gates: eval suite shows no more than 2% degradation in answer accuracy/F1 on critical prompt set.
Automated rollback rehearsal executes in staging and validates that traffic routing and KV cache rebuild complete within SLOs.
Generated runbook includes root-cause hints and automatically links to the failing test logs and the candidate build artifacts.
risk_assessment: Medium - simulator reduces human error but introduces additional CI time and flakiness risk if synthetic workloads are not representative. We'll mitigate by starting as opt-in and restricting runs to dedicated staging pools.
mitigation_plan: 1) Conservative default thresholds with ability to tune per-channel; 2) Canary the simulator on non-production releases for 2 weeks; 3) Add synthetic workload calibration job that compares simulator traffic to sampled production traces weekly.
notes: Decision: use existing compatibility prober infra (ENG-31207) and extend it with perf/eval hooks rather than building a separate agent. We will reuse the synthetic workload repo and add a KV warmup subroutine. Trade-off: longer CI runtime vs. fewer post-release incidents.
